brief.title: RC Answers: Use a Proof-Before-Pick Method to Reject Trap Options
brief.seoTitle: Reading Comprehension Trap Answers: Proof-Before-Pick Method
brief.description: Learn how to validate reading comprehension answers with a proof-before-pick method. Test every option for contradiction, scope, evidence, inference distance, and wording precision before selecting it.
secondaryKeywords: how to eliminate wrong answers in reading comprehension
brief.readerProblem: Students choose options because they sound reasonable, repeat passage language, or express a real-world truth—even when the passage contradicts them, does not support them, or makes a narrower claim.
brief.contentAngle: Teach an auditable answer-verification protocol rather than a general elimination list. Readers must prove that an option fits the question and passage before selecting it.
brief.uniqueValue: The article will pair each trap type with an original mini-passage, question, attractive wrong option, and proof-based rejection. The central sequence—contradiction, scope, evidence, inference distance, and wording precision—helps readers distinguish a supported answer from one that merely sounds plausible.
outline: What a proof-before-pick method means in reading comprehension
Step 1: Identify exactly what the question is asking
Step 2: Test for direct contradiction with the passage
Step 3: Check whether the option stays within the passage’s scope
Step 4: Demand evidence for every important part of the option
Step 5: Measure inference distance and reject unsupported leaps
Step 6: Inspect wording precision, including absolute and comparative terms
How to handle options that reuse the passage’s exact language
How to compare two plausible options using the stronger proof
Original worked examples across main idea, inference, detail, tone, and application questions
A timed proof-before-pick checklist and error-log format
How the method transfers across CAT, XAT, GMAT, GRE, CLAT, IPMAT, SSC, and Banking-style RC questions

factConstraints: Use the supplied SERP URLs only as external references; verify every page and its current claims before publication.
Do not present supplied SERP snippets as independently verified research until a human reviewer checks the linked pages.
Do not claim that any trap type appears at a particular frequency or that the method guarantees a score increase; no such statistics were supplied.
Keep the framework exam-agnostic, and label exam-specific differences only when supported by verified official or supplied sources.
Create original passages, questions, answer choices, and worked explanations; do not reproduce copyrighted exam questions or third-party examples.
For every worked example, explicitly show the passage claim, the option’s wording, the failed proof check, and the corrected choice if applicable.
Require human review for factual accuracy, exam terminology, answer keys, originality, and alignment with the linked source material before publication.
Avoid implying that outside knowledge is always irrelevant; explain that the answer must be justified by the passage when the question is passage-based.
Use only the supplied internal URLs for internal linking, with natural anchors and no invented page destinations.
Review for cannibalization against existing broad CAT reading-comprehension strategy and accuracy pages; preserve this article’s narrower proof-based intent.
